MGMT 3345 Unit 1 Project

STEP 1 #Complete this step in Excel.

Real returns were calculated in Excel using the CPI-deflation method:

Real Return (%) = ( (P_t / P_t-1) / (CPI_t / CPI_t-1) - 1 ) * 100

Per the project instructions, the CPI for October 2025 was set to the Treasury Department’s contingency index of 325.604 (BLS did not release an official October 2025 CPI due to the government shutdown). See the “Source Data” tab of Fidelity_Real_Returns.xlsx for the priced/CPI inputs and the “Fidelity” tab for the resulting 58 real-return observations (Feb 2021 - Nov 2025).

Import the completed real returns file for use in the remaining steps.

# Update this path if your file lives somewhere else on your machine.
df <- read_excel("data/Fidelity_Real_Returns.xlsx", sheet = "Fidelity")

# Row 1 (Jan 2021) has no prior month price, so it has no real return.
# Drop it, leaving the 58 monthly real-return observations (Feb 2021-Nov 2025).
df <- df[-1, ]

str(df)

STEP 2 #Descriptive statistics

funds <- c("Consumer_Staples", "Energy", "Financials",
           "Health_Care", "Information_Technology", "Utilities")

fund_mean <- sapply(df[funds], mean)
fund_sd   <- sapply(df[funds], sd)

descriptive_stats <- data.frame(
  Fund               = funds,
  `Monthly Return (Mean)` = round(fund_mean, 4),
  `Standard Deviation`    = round(fund_sd, 4),
  check.names = FALSE
)

descriptive_stats

Copy these mean and standard deviation values (rounded to 4 decimal places) into the Step 2a table in the Word document.

STEP 4 #Portfolios

Each portfolio invests 40% in the first fund listed and 60% in the second fund listed.

portfolio <- function(x, y, w1 = 0.4, w2 = 0.6) {
  rho <- cor(x, y)
  exp_return <- w1 * mean(x) + w2 * mean(y)
  variance <- (w1^2) * var(x) + (w2^2) * var(y) + 2 * w1 * w2 * cov(x, y)
  std_dev <- sqrt(variance)

  round(c(
    Correlation      = rho,
    `Expected Return` = exp_return,
    Variance         = variance,
    `Standard Deviation` = std_dev
  ), 4)
}
# Portfolio 1: Health_Care (40%) / Information_Technology (60%)
portfolio(df$Health_Care, df$Information_Technology)
       Correlation    Expected Return           Variance Standard Deviation 
            0.4119             1.1481            32.9008             5.7359 
# Portfolio 2: Energy (40%) / Utilities (60%)
portfolio(df$Energy, df$Utilities)
       Correlation    Expected Return           Variance Standard Deviation 
            0.3199             1.1797            25.0023             5.0002 
# Portfolio 3: Consumer_Staples (40%) / Financials (60%)
portfolio(df$Consumer_Staples, df$Financials)
       Correlation    Expected Return           Variance Standard Deviation 
            0.5605             0.9542            30.7020             5.5409
